identity: In ANY local product basis respecting the separate 2+2 reducing subspaces, H=X†X is the orthogonal direct sum of four 4×4 PSD sectors Hi. Write Ti=ρ(|Hi^[2]|) and Ri=ρ(|Hi|), and let R(1),R(2) be the two largest of the four Ri. The full 120×120 modulus compound decomposes into four within-sector blocks |Hi^[2]| and six cross-sector blocks |Hi|⊗I4+I4⊗|Hj|, up to signed permutations. Hence EXACTLY ρ(|H^[2]|)=max(max_i Ti, R(1)+R(2)). This holds even when Hi themselves are reducible, because the formula uses the whole four-dimensional sectors.
remaining_gap: For the 2+2 class, one sufficient route to f274 membership is to construct some reducing-block-respecting bases with every Ti≤2L and R(1)+R(2)≤2L. The first violating inequality in all block-respecting bases would still NOT imply η>2L, because η also permits arbitrary local unitaries mixing the reducing subspaces. A genuine optimized obstruction must cover ALL such bases. The recently constructed original pair fails in one block-respecting basis but has a different explicit strict-certificate basis.
scope: Only block decomposition/Kronecker Perron identity; no proof the inequalities always hold and no global T2/T3/Z2/q3 or physical counterexample.
